---
title: "Accessibility statement"
---

This statement applies to the Computing with AI course site, the reading copy of
the course material. It was prepared and last reviewed on 25 November 2026.

We want everyone on the module to be able to use this site. We aim to meet the
Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, WCAG 2.2, level AA, which is the later
version of the guidelines that EN 301 549 references at level 2.1 AA.

## What you can expect

- Every page states its language, and passages in Chinese are marked as Chinese
  so that a screen reader pronounces them correctly. The bilingual glossary is
  marked up as a real table with a header row, so each Chinese term stays
  joined to the English term and the explanation beside it rather than being
  read out as a run of loose text.
- The colour pairs defined in the site's stylesheet meet the AA contrast ratios
  (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for interface boundaries and focus indicators) in both
  the light and the dark theme. We also measured every piece of visible text on
  every page, in both themes and at two window widths, against the colour
  actually painted behind it rather than against the colour the stylesheet
  declares: 1,708 measurements, the lowest of them 4.57:1, and none below the
  ratio that applies to it. You can switch theme with the toggle on each page.
- On the home page, every link, button and the search box can be reached with
  the Tab key in an order that follows the page, and each shows the same
  visible focus indicator: a 3 pixel ring with a 2 pixel gap, measured at no
  less than 7.4:1 in the light theme and 11.4:1 in the dark one against the
  grounds it appears on. A "skip to main content" link is the first stop, and
  no stop was off the screen. Other pages use the same layout and components
  but we have not walked them one by one.
- Links in the body text are underlined as well as coloured, so colour is not the
  only cue.
- We checked the heading levels on every page and none skips a level. Pages that
  have section headings also have an in-page contents list; short pages without
  section headings do not.
- Every notebook is published as an ordinary web page of text, code and output,
  not as an image or an embedded viewer.
- We measured the width of every page, with the browser window set to 640
  pixels wide (as a 1280 pixel window at 200% zoom would be) and to 320 pixels
  (400%), in both themes, and none needs sideways scrolling. This was a
  window-width emulation, not real browser zoom. Code blocks and code output
  are not counted, because they scroll inside their own box. Everything else is
  counted: the glossary's three columns wrap at 320 pixels instead of becoming a
  strip that scrolls sideways, and a long URL or file path written in the text
  wraps rather than pushing the page out from under you.

## Known limitations

This is our current position, and we will update it as the site changes.

- **Not yet independently audited, and testing so far is limited.** On
  25 November 2026 we measured colour contrast and reflow on all eleven pages,
  in both themes and at both 640 and 320 pixels, and walked the home page with
  the Tab key in both themes, all in one Chromium-based browser. The
  measurements were taken by a script that runs inside the page, and that
  script is in the course repository (`scripts/audit_site_a11y.py`), so the
  numbers above can be regenerated rather than taken on trust. We did not walk
  every page with the keyboard (the others share the home page's layout and
  components), did not test text-only zoom, other browsers, or any screen
  reader, and did not run a full audit with assistive technology. We therefore
  describe the site as partially compliant.
- **Stage pages.** Every stage is listed in the sidebar, but the stages that
  have no published notebooks yet are listed without being linked: their names
  render as plain text rather than as links. Their landing pages can still be
  reached through the previous and next links at the foot of the page.
- **Charts and images in notebooks** (WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content). A figure
  produced by code may not have a text description. Where a figure carries
  information, the surrounding text or the code that draws it is meant to give
  the same information; where it does not, that is a fault we want to hear
  about.
- **Interactive widgets are not yet published.** The module will add
  interactive explanations. Each will be built from ordinary page elements rather
  than a drawing canvas, will work with a keyboard (for example arrow keys for a
  slider), and will have a text version that presents the same information as a
  table or as prose. This statement will be updated when the first one ships.
- **Code output** (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow). A table printed by code, and a long
  line of output, scroll sideways inside their own box rather than reflowing.
  That is deliberate: squeezing a printed table's columns until a date wraps
  over three lines destroys the alignment that is the point of printing it.
  Tables written in the text reflow; this applies only to what code prints.

## Tell us about a problem

If you cannot use part of this site, or you need the material in another format,
tell the module teaching team. Say which page it is and what you were trying to
do.

## TODO before publication: name the responsible body, and give a contact

Two things are missing from this statement, and it is incomplete until both are
supplied. The module lead must:

1. **Name the institution that publishes this site.** The affiliation was taken
   out of the public pages while the site is being tested. The duty under the
   UK Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) Accessibility
   Regulations 2018 attaches to the body that publishes a site, not to whether
   the page prints its name, so taking the name out did not remove the
   obligation: it removed the reader's means of finding out who is answerable
   for it. Naming the institution again restores the citation of those
   Regulations, and with it the enforcement route that was removed alongside
   the name -- the Equality Advisory and Support Service (EASS) in Great
   Britain, and the Equality Commission for Northern Ireland in Northern
   Ireland. A page that names nobody cannot honestly send a reader to a
   regulator, which is why that paragraph is not here now.
2. **Give a real contact** -- an email address, or the course repository's issue
   tracker -- and state any response time they are willing to commit to.

Do not publish this statement until both are done.
:::

## Technical information

This site is built with Quarto and is intended for publication on GitHub Pages.
It has not been deployed yet, so every check described above was made against a
copy of the site rendered on a local machine, not against a live address. We
will review this statement once it is published.

It relies on HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Its accessibility depends on these
technologies working with your browser and any assistive technology you use.
